79: Three things decide it: pile, backing, color. Pile that still springs back, a solid backing, and a color you can live with add up to a $99-per-room stretch rather than a new floor. Crushed traffic lanes, seams pulling open, backing turning to powder, or odor that outlasted a professional cleaning point the other way. Si View bungalows and Forster Woods two-stories land on both sides of that line, so we look before quoting.
83: Start underneath. Odor that never leaves starts in the subfloor, not in the carpet on top of it, so the first defense is a moisture-barrier pad — an upgrade that runs $0.65 per square foot and up. Over that goes solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing: pigment locked inside the fiber, so diluted bleach lifts a stain without lifting the color. Around here, where the dog comes back from Little Si caked to the knees, that pairing earns its price.
85: Two separate warranties, and both get written onto your quote. The mill's covers the carpet itself — wear and stain, 10 to 25 years depending on the grade you buy. Ours covers the labor: a 1-year workmanship warranty from OC Flooring, the same on a river-road cabin as on a subdivision two-story. One catch — mills sometimes tie coverage to the pad grade underneath, which is why all three grades ride along to the appointment.
